summary: Residence-based reservation in PG medical courses held unconstitutional; precedent from Pradeep Jain and Saurabh Chaudri reaffirmed; domicile criteria violate Article 14; institutional preference permissible but residence-based quotas impermissible; State Quota seats to be filled by NEET merit; impugned reservation policy struck down.
legal_provisions_cited: Jagadish Saran v. Union of India (1980) 2 SCC 768
Dr. Pradeep Jain v. Union of India (1984) 3 SCC 654
Saurabh Chaudri v. Union of India (2003) 11 SCC 146
final_judgment: Appeal allowed; High Court decision upheld; residence-based reservation quashed; admissions to be based on NEET merit.
